chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) narrating to Ata'a, saying: The length of the ark of Noah was one thousand and two hundred cubits, and its width was eight hundred cubits, and its height in the sky was two hundred cubits. It circumambulated the House (Ka'ba) and performed sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwa seven circuits, then it rested upon Mount Judi.

key_terms.السَّعْي: Sa'y — the ritual walking or running seven times between al-Safa and al-Marwa during Hajj
key_terms.الطَّوَاف: Circumambulation (tawaf) — the ritual of circling the Ka'ba seven times during Hajj or Umra
key_terms.الْجُودِيّ: Mount Judi — the mountain where Noah's ark rested, mentioned in Quran 11:44
key_terms.ذِرَاع: Cubit — a unit of measurement based on the length of the forearm, approximately 45-50 cm
key_terms.سَفِينَةُ نُوحٍ: Ark of Noah — the vessel built by Prophet Noah (AS) during the great flood

ai.seo_question: What were the dimensions of Noah's ark according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports from his father Imam al-Baqir (AS) a remarkable narration about Noah's ark (peace be upon him) — that it was colossal in dimensions and, remarkably, performed the ritual circumambulation (tawaf) of the Ka'ba and the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwa before coming to rest upon Mount Judi. This hadith, transmitted in the context of a chapter on the Hajj of the Prophets, highlights the ancient and sacred nature of these rites, asserting that even the ark of Noah participated in the primordial Hajj rituals, linking cosmological events to the sacred geography of Mecca.
